The consensus thesis assumes that the aggressive ramp in capital expenditures—guided to an unprecedented $130 billion to $145 billion annual envelope—will generate high-return advertising yield enhancements through Advantage+ and conversational commerce, comfortably outpacing infrastructure depreciation, elevated power expenses, and stock-based compensation.

However, this premium valuation establishes significant asymmetric vulnerability. It discounts minimal friction from structural headwinds: severe operating margin compression from infrastructure buildouts, Reality Labs operating losses exceeding $16 billion annually, AI compute inflation, and potential deceleration in standalone consumer AI applications such as Muse. With an owner cash yield of just 2.3%, the equity is exposed to sharp multiple contraction upon any deceleration in advertising yield or CapEx overextension.
